name: DEEP FRACTURE: Lives of the Wired Poor
description: The most recent and most controversial entry-level full-neural sim to achieve mainstream attention, DEEP FRACTURE immerses players in three interconnected Tier 1 lives — a debt-bonded chrome-worker, a synth-protein distribution clerk, and an unlicensed BCI technician — with sensory and economic fidelity calibrated to actual Shelf living conditions sourced from anonymous BCI data contributions by real Tier 1 residents. Released by a Tier 2 cooperative called Ground Signal under a pay-what-you-can model, it has been called both the most important social document in neural gaming history and an exploitative spectacle. Tier 4-5 critics and Tier 1 residents have almost exactly opposite opinions about which.
story_hooks: One of DEEP FRACTURE's three playable lives is too specific — and a Tier 1 resident recognizes it as their own, down to details no anonymized dataset should contain.

A Tier 5 corponation executive has played DEEP FRACTURE forty times and has been quietly transferring funds to Ground Signal anonymously — their assistant has figured out why and doesn't know what to do with the information.

The unlicensed BCI technician character keeps accessing a hidden fourth narrative thread that Ground Signal says doesn't exist in their build — and the content of what players find there suggests it's being written in real time by someone inside the game.
